HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON character-introduction splash PAINTED like bidam-defiance: oil-glazed volume on the face, one hard key raking the cheek, crushed shadow on the far side, intro-card splash, emotionally revealing, visceral, movie-worth — not a flat cel headshot, not a catalogue 3/4 portrait. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). INTIMATE ECU of ONE character: the FACE fills the central band of the 2:1 crop, larger than a usual close-up, eyes and mouth razor-sharp, placed off-centre on a third with a slight dutch. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. KOREAN FACE: living eyes — WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, never the entire eyeball painted solid black). Low soft Korean nasal bridge. Keep identity from the attached sheet but REDRAW a NEW expression; the sheet's smile or smirk is not this beat.
